quotes.excerpt: The Dirt Beneath the Devil #1 is an amazing opening issue for the series that will surely trap readers’ interest in reading more of the series. The mysteries that this issue either straight out tells us or implies are enough to peek even the most jaded readers’ interest. The premise that is laid out here in the first issue is intriguing, but when you know that Panosian obviously has more in store for us that jacks the intrigued levels all the way up. This should be a slam dunk pick up at the shop or Neon Ichiban this week. As a matter of fact, make sure to add this one to your Pull List as you won’t want to miss a single issue of this series.
The Dirt Beneath the Devil #1 is a solid debut issue. It takes a familiar concept and puts it in a setting that feels rather new and fresh.

Witness Point #1 succeeds because it understands that a great crime story needs more than a clever premise. Nathan Fillon and Heath Corson build a small town full of personalities, grudges, secrets, and simmering tension, while artist Soo Lee gives every character enough individuality to make them feel like a suspect, a victim, or both. The witness protection angle provides an irresistible foundation, but the issue never relies solely on its elevator pitch. Instead, it carefully constructs a mystery populated by colorful characters, sharp dialogue, and just enough chaos, including a tiger attack, to keep readers on their toes. If the series can maintain this level of plotting and characterization, Witness Point has all the ingredients to become one of the year's standout crime comics.

I’ve always been a fan of mob stories, both fiction and non-fiction. So when we kick right off with a mob hit, I was sucked in. However, despite the title of the book, the path the story took was one I didn’t see coming. This is not your Tony Soprano, Vito Corleone, or Henry Hill type of story (well, maybe Henry Hill at the end of Goodfellas). This is unique and different. It’s filled with mystery, a few smiles, and a desire to know what the hell is going on.

The Infernal Hulk #10 is a powerful close to the opening act of the Infernal Hulk War. Phillip Kennedy Johnson delivers big story movement, smart character choices, and enough unresolved tension to make the next chapter feel essential. Adam Gorham and Matthew Wilson match that energy with brutal, eerie, and epic visuals that keep the horror tone alive on every page. This issue gives the arc a satisfying sense of payoff while making the road ahead feel even more exciting. If you were not following along as this series dropped, make sure to keep your eyes open for when the Trade hits the shelves. Also, keep your eyes open for the FOC for March to Hulk War: Infernal Hulk vs Wolverine #1 as you won’t want to miss that one either!
The Infernal Hulk #10 continues the exciting story with a bit of a horror energy that brings the energy level up to an all time high.

Eddie attempts to be a reluctant hero as Trent is kidnapped in another phenomenal issue. Starks unloads the deep rooted feelings in-between the adult humor. Pugh & O'Halloran bring the insanity of Eddie’s world to spectacular life. There is no good reason End Of Life shouldn’t be in your collection.

This issue is pretty close to perfect, but it also seems to bring an end to the whole Pluto era of the title. I’m very curious to see where it goes now, as the small-town setting was one of the big selling points.

Conan The Barbarian #33 sets sail when Conan and the Red Brotherhood are shipwrecked on a mysterious island after encountering a massive storm and a supernatural attacker. Jim Zub’s start to the latest arc is as strong as ever, and Fernando Dagnino’s artwork is a perfect fit. 10 out of 10. No notes.

Land of Never #1 is a nice start to a very promising series. The initial premise will grab your attention, but the teased tie in will make you sit up in your seat. The artwork is fantastic and leaves nothing to the imagination as it captures the story completely. This is a must grab at the shop this week. Give this first issue a shot and consider adding it to your Pull List, or at the very least order the second issue to see where it goes.

Land of Never takes a familiar tale and twists it into something truly unsettling. Steve Orlando delivers a gripping mystery fueled by a desperate father, all while Miguel Mora illustrates atmospheric tension that jumps from the page. Land of Never is the version of an age-old classic that you never knew you needed, a blend of heart and horror. Cannot wait for what is coming next.

The Smart Division is a fantastic science-fiction mystery that eerily could be more fact than fiction. Writer Zack Kaplan delivers a timely detective tale exploring the use of modern technology in solving crimes. However, it’s the juxtaposition of John Pearson’s elegant brush strokes that makes story rise above the rest. Kaplan and Pearson’s creativity knows no bounds and The Smart Division is proof of that.

I sat down with The Smart Division expecting a slick sci-fi detective story and walked away rattled about the world outside my window. That is the highest thing I can say about a comic right now. This is a perfect debut and one of the most relevant books on the stands, and I cannot wait to see where the case goes.
Power Rangers: Green #1 delivers a unique take on the post-apocalyptic story, and a new version of Tommy Oliver.

This debut issue brings back an iconic original Ranger in a futuristic setting. No longer a practicing Ranger, but the last Ranger in existence. Teaming up with an old foe to take on a new threat that is bringing Tommy out of retirement. This issue doesn’t answer some of the more pivotal questions surrounding Tommy, but it paints a comforting picture that he is living a more simplistic life. This is a must-read for Power Ranger fans! So make sure you pick up your copy of this new miniseries and add this to your “pull list.”A little bonus for this review! I had the opportunity to speak with Pallie Paul Allor about this issue as well as what readers can expect in issue two. If you are a fan of Alpha, you are going to want to see what he does in this debut issue because it leads to much more from him physically in issue two!

Superman #40 wraps up one big event, leads us into another, and hints at the future for Superboy Prime. With Clark Kent set to return soon, Prime won’t be front and center, but I think he’s shown that he can be a more than average substitute for the Man of Steel.
Williamson, Mora and Sanchez roll the dice in walking a fine line of genius and insanity with CK’s heroic methods. Another display of high level storytelling for a very polarizing character.

FINAL GRADE: 9.8The Suns ride again into the belly of the beast with a non-stop thrilling adventure. MacKay steers events into a surprise twist ending, but the art steals the show on this one. Pramanik & Rosenberg present a magnificent display of combat & drama. You won’t be ready for what unfolds here!

It’s all hands on deck as ‘Marc Spector: Moon Knight’ #6 brings back a classic Marvel team to help the moonlit vigilante save his family. Marvel canon is woven perfectly into a modern tale as the visuals turn the dial all the way to eleven once more.

This is a perfect debut and one of the most relevant books on the stands, and I cannot wait to see where the case goes.

Operation: Iron Coffin comes out of the gate swinging with a unique premise that delivers far more than ever expected. Kenny Porter and Tyrell Cannon give us a Dracula that isn’t just here for the carnage, although we get plenty of that, but for a compelling redemption arc wrapped in a fast-paced, blood-soaked WWII setting. IDW Dark may have some heavy hitting titles in its first year as an imprint at IDW Publishing, but Operation: Iron Coffin stands out as one of the best.

Operation Coffin #1 is a stylish debut for Porter and Cannon’s new take on Dracula. A truly unique premise, backed by engaging lore and a curious mission have already laid the groundwork for a wild ride ahead.

While this series has just four issues and that might not seem like a lot of space to tell such an intense tale, The Horror of Godzilla #1 has already set things up for horrific greatness. You’re never going to look at the King of the Monsters the same way again.

The Horror of Godzilla #1 is exactly what the title promises, an incredibly terrifying look at the King of the Monsters through the eyes of those caught in their path. Writers Ethan S. Parker and Griffin Sheridan deliver on of the most unsettling Godzilla stories I have ever experienced, while Tristan Jones brings his A-game with artwork that is both impactful and horrifying. The Horror of Godzilla is one of the most frightening Godzilla stories with some of the best illustrations I have seen in recent memory, making it a strong contender for comic of the year.

A tragic past reveal sparks an explosive search for present day answers as Batman is on the hunt! Taylor pens a striking tale of loss and heart in this latest chapter. Janín exposes the a hero’s last moments with stunning art. This series never falters on delivering high marks.
Detective Comics #1111 ramps up the action and mystery in the latest issue, while also showcasing the great potential of having Batman team up with additional heroes.

The Uncanny X-Men #32 brings this out-of-this-world arc to an end and we’re left on a very interesting note of uncertainty, sadness, and love. Gail Simone makes you feel every emotion and leaves you wanting more.

When the Nur try wiping out the Brood, they forgot what party they crashed! Simone’s writing balances the heartfelt drama with outright fun themes. The art centers in on the chaotic scene with great success. This has been such a refreshing change of pace story that reminds fans to push the creative boundaries on the stat quo X-tales.

An origin story centered around one of the main book’s killers could have easily gone sideways, but thankfully that’s simply not the case with Rascal Randy. Instead, fans have an up-close look at several compelling characters and insight into one of the most unpredictable and twisted characters in comics.

If you finished Exquisite Corpses Season 1 wanting more from Rascal Randy, this new series is exactly what you had hope for. Tyler Boss expands on the history of the character without taking away some of the mystery in the main series. Boss delivers a creepy, atmospheric story that stands confidently on its own while adding to the lore Exquisite Corpses. Exquisite Corpses: Rascal Randy is one of those rare prequels that doesn’t just justify its existence, it makes an already iconic character even more fascinating.

The Flash #35 is another winning chapter that reminds readers why Wally West remains one of DC's most endearing heroes. Ryan North balances inventive superhero concepts with genuine heart, while Gavin Guidry's artwork radiates personality from start to finish. The central idea of preventing disasters before they happen opens up exciting possibilities, and the creative team wisely leaves enough uncertainty to keep you wondering where it all leads. Even before the larger questions arrive, this issue succeeds by making heroism feel joyful, hopeful, and endlessly fun.

Wally West’s obsession with the future leads to more hijinks as events speed along. North leans heavily into the scientific portion of plans with the writing. Guidry and Lucas craft solid looks at this new scheme via the art. An interesting take leading into more fast problems down the road. Don’t miss out.

I’m sure some of the rhetoric in this issue, particularly out of Mia’s mouth, will get a lot of people talking about certain real-world parallels, but this comic actually works really well justin the context of a superhero story. This is a world where the innocent are hunted and the guilty are more powerful than ever, and the heroes are often powerless to strike back – so villain tactics might be necessary to fight back.

Absolute Green Arrow #2 takes us deeper into the mystery of who our killer is. This issue brings us to familiar faces within the Green Arrow lore and shrouds us in mystery even more than before. The blend of action and suspense is working cleverly, making this a horror story of sorts. I will have this run at the very top of my pull pile every month; I hope it gets expanded beyond its current limited run.

Overall, to say issue #1 of Chachu is brilliant would be selling it short. Iman Vellani has crafted something genuinely beautiful, bold and gutsy here. It’s the kind of debut that isn’t to be missed. It’s not just a showcase for her sharp mind for this style of art and storytelling. Still, every single frame is brought to life so gorgeously by Marianna Ignazzi that it’s hard to look away, and the story setup, characters and plot points being woven together are as good as first issues get. For the art of the craft, you need to do yourself a favour and pick up a copy of this comic; it demands your attention.
Right when i was done reading this book, I'm like “I want more!” I want the second issue right now! If you're not picking up Chachu #1, you need to change that! Get into your car, go

From the deep messages and fantastic storytelling to the excellent and varied art & colors, “Justice League Dream Girls” continues to astound! Maines and Axelrod continue to prove they put their souls into their writing while Wilson more than delivers on a fantastic Harlivy side story. This is a fantastic series that you won’t want to miss!

The interaction between Galaxy and the 1st transgender superhero Coagula is an utterly iconic mentoring and banter moment and truly empowers Galaxy to speak up for herself and Dreamer. It’s also a lovely homage to Coagula’s co-creator, the late Rachel Pollack. It’s also so damn relatable that Galaxy is overwhelmed by all the screens around her: a true superhero vulnerability for 2026.

Walter makes a choice that shakes the remaining survivors to their core in this pen-ultimate chapter. Tynion hones in on the emotional tears into the groups while orchestrating the horrors. Bueno and Bellaire give a chilling insight into reactions with magnificent art. The end is here….who will survive?

The Nice House by the Sea #11 expertly positions every major player for what promises to be an unforgettable finale. James Tynion IV balances emotional breakthroughs, unsettling horror, and escalating stakes with remarkable confidence, while Álvaro Martínez Bueno continues to deliver some of the most inventive visuals in comics. With relationships changing, long-buried truths coming to light, and the biodomes themselves becoming an active threat, the series heads into its final issue with tremendous momentum.

Poseidon vs. Aquaman…get ready to rumble! Adams pens a rock’em, sock’em showdown for the ages. Timms and Lokus go from broke with sensational action sequences. A thrilling look at the evolution of Arthur Curry! Don’t miss it!

While the ongoing plot of the Atlantean Empire and the villain team up takes a backseat, Emperor Aquaman #20 presents us with a surprisingly thrilling battle between hero and god that continues the interpersonal drama of Aquaman's new powers.

Poke’s life after “Out-Break Day” doesn’t escape more pain and danger as events become cold. Camp deals with the scars of survival with phenomenal writing. Morian & Hollingsworth construct an incredible journey through souls in the panels. The ending page may make your heart stop as Poke’s world refuses to let go of readers!

Kara Zor-El leads the Superfamily into investigating General Zod's activities in Supergirl #16, which does a lot to show the Girl of Steel has what it takes to succeed Superman as Earth's Kryptonian hero.

Kara leads an army into hostile territory as Zod’s plans of vengeance begin! Campbell nails the impactful points while balancing the lighter moments. The art team exemplify the iconic shots heading into the conflict. Get ready for a battle of epic proportions!

Adam Gorham and Matthew Wilson match that energy with brutal, eerie, and epic visuals that keep the horror tone alive on every page. This issue gives the arc a satisfying sense of payoff while making the road ahead feel even more exciting. If you were not following along as this series dropped, make sure to keep your eyes open for when the Trade hits the shelves. Also, keep your eyes open for the FOC for March to Hulk War: Infernal Hulk vs Wolverine #1 as you won’t want to miss that one either!
The Infernal Hulk #10 continues the exciting story with a bit of a horror energy that brings the energy level up to an all time high.

This issue sets us up for a big finale! I cannot get enough of how gorgeous the art style is within these pages, and the emotion is charged with Lorraine making a last desperate attempt to save Ronnie. If nothing else, the cover alone should sell you on this issue and tell you why you need to be picking this book up!

All eyes are on Pittsburgh as Firehawk makes one last attempt to save Ronnie Raymond. Lemire keeps the thrills at a high level for this chapter. De Latorre & Maiolo wave strong art throughout the mass chaos. Expect that last page to generate some chatter at the LCS.

Over the years, Monstress has fallen victim to the numbing complexity of so much high fantasy. Its greatest strength is its deeper darkness, which is embraced quite well in the 63rd issue of the series. There’s still a lot of clutter in the narrative that really could be removed to allow the more powerful moments more of a chance to resonate, but it’s a fun 63rd issue.

It’s not talked about enough how incredibly different Gail Simone makes each issue of The Uncanny X-Men, and each issue is a winner. The Uncanny X-Men #33 is high in emotion and wrapped in layers of different depths. Right now, every character is carrying their own issues, and we get to empathize with each one of them and feel what they feel. That’s the magic of Simone’s writing: she allows the reader to have a personal connection with the characters, making us feel closer and closer to them and the story.

Gambit’s running out of time as his curse now requires some supernatural help! Simone’s writing showcases the impact of new leaders trying to guide the next generation.. The art delivers on presenting the chilling truths of Gambit’s case with strong art. This story has a new aura looming around it that readers won’t want to miss.

This continues to be my favorite Captain America run. Captain America #14 is such a unique take on the dichotomy between Doom and Steve Rogers. It gives us a version of Steve Rogers that wears his heart on his sleeve, stands up for the little guy, and admits his own faults and shortcomings.
Captain America #14 is a reminder of how power can twist the soul, but also reminds readers that certain souls are far more complex than they seem.

The Spectre’s rage is finally settled, but at what cost? Lemire presents a strong closing chapter with much emotion behind it. Olortegui & Guerrero delve into the heavy burden with impressive images. A consistent reminder of what superhero stories are all about.

This is the new standard. Not every Marvel character that hits a major milestone will be able to use time travel to tell their story, but Fantastic Four #15 is the playbook for a new way forward in telling the history of characters without relying simply on anthology style stories. Fantastic Four is fun, daring, unique, and rewriting all the rules in the best ways possible. Instant Classic!

A time traveling tale that honors the legacy of Marvel’s first family 65 years readers won’t want to put down. North takes this saga into a few unique places before leading to a superb finish. Ramos and the art team deliver excellent images fitting for the celebration at hand. It’s been a hell of a ride for 65 and here’s to many more!
This series is a wonderful, nostalgic romp through Iron Man’s past foes that also builds a satisfying mystery for new readers! This is another home run for the incredible creative team!

Iron Man #8 demonstrates that Joshua Williamson has a clear long-term vision for Tony Stark. Rather than resolving conflicts quickly, the series continues layering mysteries involving Madame Masque, AIM, Citizen V, and the School of Super-Science, making each chapter feel like an important piece of a larger puzzle. Carmen Carnero's energetic artwork elevates every fight, particularly the revamped Whiplash encounter, while clever visual storytelling keeps the momentum high. The issue may focus more on moving pieces into place than delivering major revelations, but the confidence of its storytelling makes the journey increasingly rewarding.

reason.snippet: Hans and Gillen expertly introduce the power players who populate the world of DIE. From the explicitly announced to the completely unexpected, they're welcome complications.
pros: The way Hans frames her characters echoes the comic's exploration of the world's bigger picture. It's gorgeous, subtle comics craft.
Hans' expressions are unmatched, particularly the one that closes this issue. It's hysterical, horrible, and completely fitting for the character who makes it.
The power players Gillen reintroduces are intriguing to the last. It's exciting to see them take the stage. It will be interesting to see how they interact with…

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: ‘Jeff the Land Shark: Superstar’ #2 is a cute and fun issue that all ages will enjoy. Kelly Thompson manages to add a touch of important social commentary about reality TV without it seeming out of place. Tokitokoro and Jim Campbell do an amazing job with the artwork and manage to capture all of the cuteness that comes with a Jeff the Land Shark comic.
pros: Kelly Thompson manages to insert some social commentary about reality TV in a way that feels natural
Tokitokoro and Jim Campbell anime-esque style captures the cuteness of a Jeff the Land Shark comic perfectly without being a direct 1:1 of the Infinity Comics
Tokitokoro's use of the chibi heads adds a creative and interesting visual dynamic in certain panels.
Jeff being protective explaining what it means to be a hero a heartwarming side to him that we don't see often.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: A scattershot of subplots that are all enjoyable, but struggle to stand out amongst themselves in such a confined number of pages.
pros: Maintains the high standard of characterization, art, and intrigue
cons: Lacks a sense of focus that makes it feel overstuffed

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: This new Star Trek #1 feels ambitious from the start, pairing Seven of Nine with a crew steeped in franchise history before sending them toward genuinely uncharted territory. Christopher Cantwell takes time to establish the emotional lives of the crew, plants mysteries for later, and gives the central mission a wonderfully strange science-fiction hook. Dennis Menheere elevates it all with gorgeous…
pros: Seven of Nine is a compelling choice to command the Enterprise G
Strong use of Star Trek history without getting overwhelmed by nostalgia
The new region of space offers an exciting mystery with intriguing rules
Dennis Menheere delivers stunning double-page layouts and atmospheric visuals
cons: A full appreciation of the issue will require knowing the characters.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Crowbound #1 is a haunting, beautifully constructed debut from Jeff Lemire and Dustin Nguyen. The simplicity of Rose's motivation gives the strange dystopian world an immediate emotional center, while the supernatural elements offer just enough mystery to make its larger mythology enticing. Nguyen's restrained colors and dreamlike imagery make the bleakness beautiful, and the circular structure gi…
pros: Rose and her daughter give the story an immediate emotional hook
Dustin Nguyen's artwork and restrained colors are gorgeous
The Factory feels oppressive without requiring extensive exposition
cons: Much of the larger world remains intentionally vague
Familiar dystopian elements may initially remind readers of other genre stories

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: This is a great jumping on point for new readers, a brutal, bloody and thrilling story where the Punisher battles a new menace that he created.
pros: Artist Farid Karami's work is stunning and adds levels of tension to the battle scenes.
Benjamin Percy presents an interesting nemesis in Collateral Damage, a twisted man made of flesh and metal who lives to get revenge on the Punisher.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: A series of storytelling decisions plague the plot of X-Men United #6. The uneven pacing and bland characterization means that the climax of the issue falls completely flat.
pros: Some of the artwork is appropriately unsettling for an entity haunting a psychic plane of existence.
cons: The younger characters are saddled with unrefined characterization and unexciting plot beats, making their parts of the issue a drag to read.
The staging of conflict and the choices as to what beats get real estate are baffling.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Miles Morales: Spider-Man #1 puts the young web-slinger back in his Brooklyn neighborhood, pitting him against a new threat and setting up a new status quo.
pros: Hill takes Miles back down to Earth, providing a video game motif that feels in line with his generation.
Leon has the right kind of art to depict Miles' acrobatics, along with his newfound foe.
De Landro brings a more grounded, gritty approach with the flashbacks, backed by darker color hues.
cons: The personal touch of Miles writing in his journal is sorely missed.
A development that will probably recieve a mixed reception.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: While it contains the same great character work Soule has been known for in his work with the character, Fall of Kylo Ren #1 struggles to make a dramatic impact when we know the fates of the characters involved.
pros: Charles Soule continues to be able to mine a lot of interesting characters and dynamics from moments between films
Serves as an excellent follow up to the Rise of Kylo Ren and Legacy of Vader series of recent years and as a jumping on point for new readers
Soule's depictions of the various members of the First Order higher ranks and Ben Solo are all spot on
Will Sliney is one of the few comic artists who can draw the various Star Wars vehicles with ease
cons: Since this takes place between The Last Jedi and Rise of Skywalker, a lot of the dramatic tension is already gone in this issue
Sliney's art for our leads, especially Kylo, can look a little awkward as he tries to match the real life actor likenesses
The big action battle takes place off panel
Will probably make you even more annoyed at the numerous dropped narratives from Rise of Skywalker.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: The Smart Division #1 is a stellar start to a sci-fi detective story. Zack Kaplan and John J. Pearson execute the story beats to perfection, creating a delicious opening chapter.
pros: John J. Pearson's art is stunning. From the characters to the storytelling and blocking to the background and colors.
Zack Kaplan quickly creates interesting characters and a stellar plot hook that makes you immediately want the next issue.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Marc Spector: Moon Knight #7 delivers incredible artwork and character moments, making it a standout in Marvel's current catalog.
pros: Each member of the Midnight Sons gets a chance to shine.
Pramanik's artwork is some of the best you'll see in a mainsteam superhero comic.
Rosenberg's colors are both eye catching and fitting for certain characters.
A last minute twist that significantly raises the stakes for future issues.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Amazing Spider-Man #34 succeeds by balancing superhero spectacle with the small, personal moments that define Peter Parker. Joe Kelly continues to build suspense around Cormac Crane and Damage Control without giving away too much, while Ed McGuinness brings every action sequence to life with infectious energy. Although the larger story only moves forward in measured steps, the character work and v…
pros: Ed McGuinness delivers explosive, energetic action that makes the Electro battle a visual highlight.
Joe Kelly continues to make Peter Parker feel authentic through sharp humor and relatable everyday struggles.
The mystery surrounding Cormac Crane and Damage Control grows more intriguing with subtle new clues.
cons: The pacing eases off considerably as the story inches toward issue #1000.
